summary: Giuseppe Tucci was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Sapienza University of Rome under Carlo Formichi and Giovanni Vacca, and at Visva-Bharati, Dhaka, and Banaras Hindu universities. He held professorships at Sapienza and led the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East.

Giuseppe Vignato works in history/archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral studies at Peking University under Angela Falco Howard, Chongfeng Li, Su Bai, and Shichang Ma, and held an affiliation there attested in 2017.

Giyu Nishi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Hakuju Ui, Junjirō Takakusu, Masaharu Anesaki, Makoto Nagai, Taiken Kimura, and Sylvain Lévi. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1926) and Toyo University (from 1927).

Glenn H. Mullin works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Ling Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, Tenzin Gyatso, Geshe Ngawang Dhargyey, and Geshe Rabten, and founded The Mystical Arts of Tibet in 1984.
Glenn Wallis is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Masatoshi Nagatomi and traditional teacher Ross Bolleter.

Godabarish Mishra was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Ravenshaw University and the University of Calcutta, worked at Satyabadi Bana Bidyalaya and Chakradharpur High School, and served as Director at the University of Madras.

Gombojab Tsybikov was a scholar of Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Tomsk State University and Saint Petersburg State University, and served as Lecturer of the Mongolian Language at Far Eastern Federal University (~1902–1917).

Gopinath Kaviraj was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. Educated at Maharaja's College, Jaipur, and the University of Allahabad under Arthur Venis, Madhusudan Ojha, and Shashadhar Tarkachuramani, he served as librarian, Principal, and department head at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Gordon D. Kaufman worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Bethel College, Northwestern University, and Yale University. Kaufman held positions at Pomona College, Vanderbilt University, and served as Mallinckrodt Professor of Divinity at Harvard University beginning in 1963.

Gordon Hannington Luce was a scholar of history/archaeology, Sinology, and linguistics. He was educated at Dean Close School and Emmanuel College, Cambridge, and served as Professor at the University of Rangoon from circa 1920 to 1964.

Gordon Johnson is a historian of Indology who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge. He held fellowships at Trinity and Selwyn College, served as President of Wolfson College (1993–2010), Deputy Vice-Chancellor of Cambridge (1974–2010), and President of the Royal Asiatic Society (2015–2018).
Gottfried August Bürger studied at the University of Göttingen from ~1768 to 1772 and later held a post there from ~1784 to 1794.

Gottfried Ernst Groddeck was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at the Academic Gymnasium Danzig and the University of Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne, and held a post at Vilnius University from circa 1804 to 1824.

Gottfried Hermann was a scholar of linguistics who studied at Leipzig University and the University of Jena. He spent his career at Leipzig University, serving as professor of philosophy from 1798 and director of the philological seminar from 1803 to 1848.
Gottfried Kinkel was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Bonn (~1831–1834) and later held posts at the University of Bonn (~1836–1848) and ETH Zurich (~1866–1882).

Gotthilf Heinrich von Schubert was a scholar of philosophy who studied at Leipzig University and the University of Jena. He held academic posts at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (~1819–1827) and the University of Munich (~1827–1853).

Gottlieb Siegfried Bayer was a scholar of Sinology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. He studied under Christoph Theodosius Walther at the University of Königsberg and held posts at the Königsberg Public Library, Königsberg Cathedral, and the Imperial Academy of Sciences.

Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Educated at King's College London and Heidelberg University, he taught at King's College, served as Principal of Government College Lahore, and was Registrar at the University of the Punjab.

Govind Chandra Pande was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology who studied under Kshetresa Chandra Chattopadhyaya. He served as Vice-Chancellor at the University of Rajasthan, professor at the University of Allahabad, and chairman of the Allahabad Museum.

Govind Sadashiv Ghurye was an Indologist who studied at Bahauddin College, Elphinstone College, and the University of Cambridge under W. H. R. Rivers and Alfred Cort Haddon. He served as Head of Sociology at the University of Mumbai (1924–1959).
